messages.content: Now that the flights are set, price the St. Thomas hotels for the exact stay. It is one room for my wife and me, checking in Saturday, May 22 and checking out Sunday, May 30. I want the real eight-night totals, not a nightly rate that leaves out half the charges.

I rechecked those dates for two adults and one room. The most comparable available rooms are a beachfront king at Emerald Beach Resort and a king studio at the hillside Harbor Ridge Hotel. Both have refundable and advance-purchase rates. I’ll separate room charges, mandatory property charges, and tax, then account for beach transportation.
Start with Emerald Beach. Include parking even if it seems odd. Their page made it look mandatory on this offer, and I do not want it disappearing from the comparison.

For Emerald Beach’s beachfront king, the refundable rate is $369 per night. Eight nights are $2,952. The mandatory resort charge is $45 nightly, or $360, and the offer also carries an $18 nightly parking charge, or $144. Tax is $414, calculated at 12.5% on the room and resort charge. The complete refundable total is $3,870. The rate allows cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Atlantic time on May 15; after that, the penalty is the full stay.
And the nonrefundable version? Also verify that beachfront means we can actually walk from the property onto the sand.

The advance-purchase rate is $332 per night, so the room portion is $2,656. Adding the same $360 resort charge, $144 parking charge, and $377 tax gives a complete total of $3,537. It is charged in full when booked and cannot be changed or refunded. Emerald Beach has direct access to Lindbergh Bay: the beach is immediately behind the hotel, with no road crossing or shuttle required. Loungers and beach towels are covered by the resort charge, while motorized water activities cost extra.
That is a $333 difference for giving up all flexibility, correct? Now do Harbor Ridge with the same level of detail.

Correct, the Emerald advance rate saves $333 versus its refundable rate. At Harbor Ridge, the refundable king studio is $314 nightly, or $2,512 for eight nights. Its mandatory facility charge is $20 nightly, or $160. Tax at 12.5% on the room and facility charge is $334. There is no parking charge on this rate. The complete refundable total is $3,006, with penalty-free cancellation through 4:00 p.m. Atlantic time on May 18. After the deadline, the full stay is charged.
And advance purchase there?

The Harbor Ridge advance rate is $282 nightly, totaling $2,256 for the room. The facility charge is $160 and tax is $302, bringing the complete eight-night total to $2,718. Full payment is due at booking, with no refunds or date changes. That saves $288 against Harbor Ridge’s refundable rate.
Please put all four totals together before we get into whether the hillside location becomes a nuisance.

The four complete totals are: Emerald Beach refundable, $3,870; Emerald Beach advance purchase, $3,537; Harbor Ridge refundable, $3,006; and Harbor Ridge advance purchase, $2,718. The refundable Harbor Ridge stay is $864 less than refundable Emerald Beach. Even Emerald’s nonrefundable rate costs $531 more than refundable Harbor Ridge.
Good. What does Harbor Ridge’s beach transportation actually cover? I do not want to count a vague shuttle that runs once in the morning and strands us.

Harbor Ridge is not walkable to a beach. Its published schedule provides complimentary transport to Magens Bay at 9:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m., returning at 2:00 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. It also serves Sapphire Beach at 10:00 a.m., with a 3:30 p.m. return, Wednesday through Sunday. Seats must be reserved with the front desk the prior evening and are subject to capacity. On Monday and Tuesday, only the Magens Bay service operates. Beach admission, chairs, and umbrellas are not included.
So it is usable, but it controls the day. Estimate the extra transportation without pretending we know every dinner plan.

For Harbor Ridge, a reasonable allowance is $240 to $400 for the stay: roughly two taxi round trips to beaches when the shuttle timing does not work, plus four or five evening taxi outings. That would put its refundable practical total around $3,246 to $3,406. Emerald Beach eliminates beach transport and has an airport transfer of only a few minutes, but taxis for dinners or sightseeing could still add about $120 to $250. Its refundable practical total would then be roughly $3,990 to $4,120. Renting a car does not improve Emerald’s listed hotel total because the $144 parking charge is already mandatory, but rental cost, fuel, and parking elsewhere would be additional.
Check the recent ratings next. Overall scores are useful, but tell me what guests are saying about rooms, noise, service, and the beach or shuttle.

Emerald Beach currently shows 8.1 out of 10 from 412 verified stays, with 8.5 across reviews posted in the last twelve months. Recent guests consistently praise the sand access, bay views, and short airport transfer. Repeated criticisms concern aircraft noise during daytime operating hours, uneven room upkeep, and slow service when the restaurant is busy. Harbor Ridge shows 9.0 out of 10 from 286 verified stays, including 9.1 for the last twelve months. Guests frequently mention clean, spacious studios, attentive staff, and broad harbor views. The recurring drawbacks are steep paths and stairs, dependence on taxis after shuttle hours, and occasional shuttle-capacity complaints. Neither property has a material pattern of recent cleanliness complaints.
Do the room types themselves change the recommendation? We need one bed, and I care more about a functional room for eight nights than a decorative upgrade.

Harbor Ridge has the more functional room: its king studio is about 430 square feet and includes a kitchenette with a full refrigerator, microwave, two-burner cooktop, cookware, and a small dining table. Emerald’s beachfront king is about 310 square feet, with a mini-fridge and coffee maker but no microwave or kitchenette. Emerald provides a furnished balcony and direct beach proximity. For an eight-night stay, Harbor Ridge offers substantially more indoor space and makes simple breakfasts or lunches practical.
Any catches with the flight times? We land at 11:49 Saturday and fly out at 1:35 the following Sunday.

Both properties list 3:00 p.m. check-in and 11:00 a.m. checkout. On arrival, either can hold luggage if the room is not ready. Emerald is approximately five minutes from the airport; Harbor Ridge is generally a 20- to 30-minute taxi ride depending on traffic. On departure day, leaving Harbor Ridge around 10:15 a.m. would provide a sensible airport margin, while Emerald could be left closer to 10:45 a.m. Neither currently guarantees early check-in or late checkout without an additional charge.
Give me a first choice and an alternate, both refundable. No booking yet. I want the judgment to include the beach inconvenience and the review differences, not just announce the cheaper one.

First choice: Harbor Ridge’s refundable king studio at $3,006. Its stronger recent ratings, larger room, kitchenette, and $864 hotel-total advantage outweigh the lack of direct beach access. Even after a generous $400 transportation allowance, it remains about $464 below Emerald’s hotel total before Emerald’s own off-property taxis. The scheduled beach service is restrictive but credible enough to use on several days, with taxis preserving flexibility. Alternate: Emerald Beach’s refundable beachfront king at $3,870. It is the better choice if stepping directly onto the sand every day is worth the premium and daytime aircraft noise and a smaller room are acceptable. Its May 15 cancellation deadline is three days earlier than Harbor Ridge’s May 18 deadline. I have not booked or held either room; availability, totals, and cancellation terms should be checked again before purchase.
